introduction.p: For a differentiable parametric curve (x(t),y(t)), the chain rule gives dy/dx=y\prime(t)/x\prime(t) wherever x\prime(t)\ne0. We will use the coordinate derivatives to find tangents and concavity and examine points where the usual quotient is unavailable.

paragraphs.p: If x can be used as the input near t=t_0, then y changes with t through x. The chain rule says
The condition \frac{dx}{dt}\neq0 matters. If x is not changing at that instant, then a slope measured as vertical change divided by horizontal change may be infinite or may require more analysis.

exercise.title: Why is parametric slope the ratio of two time rates?

statement.p: A graph asks how fast y changes with respect to x, but a parametric curve gives rates with respect to t. In your own words, why is \dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{dy/dt}{dx/dt} the natural translation, and why must dx/dt\neq0 for that quotient to make sense?

hint.p: When x\prime(t)\ne0, divide the coordinate rates to obtain dy/dx. If x\prime(t)=0 and y\prime(t)\ne0, the tangent is vertical. If both vanish, the quotient alone cannot decide whether the curve is a graph or has a tangent.

note.title: Moral
note.p: When both dx/dt and dy/dt are zero, do not use the horizontal or vertical tangent test blindly. Study the nearby motion.

paragraphs.p: We will meet this warning again when a curve stops, reverses, or forms a cusp.

exercise.title: How do you recognize horizontal and vertical tangents parametrically?

statement.p: Horizontal tangents occur when y' is zero while x' is not; vertical tangents reverse those roles. In your own words, why do those tests match the geometry of a moving point, and why is a circle a good example of needing the parametric language?

hint.p: If the point moves only horizontally, the tangent is horizontal. A circle is not a single graph y=f(x), but its coordinate rates still determine the tangent.

statement.p: If x'(t_0)=y'(t_0)=0, the slope formula gives 0/0. In your own words, why does that not automatically mean the curve has no tangent, and what extra look nearby is required?

subsection.p: The phrase “whenever the divisions make sense” is not a minor detail. Parametric curves can have vertical tangents, cusps, and pauses. At such points, the algebra may need a separate geometric check.

exercise.title: How does plane motion package calculus into pairs?

statement.p: Position (x(t),y(t)) has velocity components x' and y'. In your own words, why is that pair already a bridge to vectors, and what does its length measure?

hint.p: Each position coordinate is an ordinary function of time. Their derivatives form the velocity pair, which points in the direction of motion when nonzero; its length is the speed.
